parts.label: (a)
parts.part_stem: A property of a vector quantity, that is not a property of a scalar quantity, is direction. For example, velocity has direction but speed does not.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: State two other scalar quantities and two other vector quantities.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: State two properties that are possessed by both scalar and vector physical quantities.

parts.label: (b)
parts.part_stem:
A ship at sea is travelling with a velocity of $13\text{ m s}^{-1}$ in a direction $35^{\circ}$ east of north in still water, as shown in Fig. 1.1.
{{figure:figure_1_1}}

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Determine the magnitudes of the components of the velocity of the ship in the north and the east directions.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
The ship now experiences a tidal current. The water in the sea moves with a velocity of $2.7\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to the west.
Calculate the resultant velocity component of the ship in the east direction.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Use your answers in (b)(i) and (b)(ii) to determine the magnitude of the resultant velocity of the ship.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text: Use your answers in (b)(i) and (b)(ii) to determine the angle between north and the resultant velocity of the ship.
